item.text: {"search_note":"I searched for Tinubu + nuclear / nuclear weapons / brinkmanship / apocalyptic language across official State House and ministry material, plus broader credible coverage, and found no direct 2024 Tinubu quote that threatens nuclear use, normalizes it, or uses nuclear saber-rattling. Because the direct nuclear record is thin, the best-supported reading is: Tinubu did not publicly use reckless nuclear rhetoric in 2024, and the only explicit nuclear-disarmament evidence is indirect through a ministerial UN statement.","evidence":[{"title":"HONOURABLE MINISTER OF DEFENCE OF NIGERIA ADDRESSES THE UNITED NATIONS ON NUCLEAR DISARMAMENT","publisher":"Ministry of Defence, Nigeria","date":"September 28, 2024","url":"https://defence.gov.ng/2024/09/28/honourable-minister-of-defence-of-nigeria-addresses-the-united-nations-on-nuclear-disarmament/","summary":"Nigeria publicly reaffirmed commitment to nuclear disarmament and non-proliferation, urged NPT compliance, endorsed the TPNW, and emphasized the catastrophic humanitarian consequences of nuclear weapon use. This is the clearest 2024 evidence of responsible nuclear rhetoric, though it comes from the defense minister rather than Tinubu himself.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu Calls for Suspension of Sanctions on Guinea, Mali, Niger, Burkina Faso","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"February 24, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubu-calls-for-suspension-of-sanctions-on-guinea-mali-niger-burkina-faso/","summary":"Tinubu urged suspension of sanctions and argued for “a better path” through negotiation and improved governance. This is not nuclear-specific, but it is relevant as de-escalatory rhetoric rather than brinkmanship.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.1"]},{"title":"President Tinubu’s Statement on the Killings of Soldiers in Aba","publisher":"State House, Nigeria","date":"June 2, 2024","url":"https://statehouse.gov.ng/president-tinubus-statement-on-the-killings-of-soldiers-in-aba/","summary":"Tinubu used strongly coercive language, saying the government would “come down heavily” and had the capacity to “crush” violent non-state actors. This is negative contextual evidence for escalation-prone rhetoric in general, but it does not involve nuclear language.","question_ids":["1B.2","1B.1"]}]}
